sentences.zh: 他在林肯包厢外面的这个小前厅里。

sentences.en: He bars the outer door behind him with a piece of wood.
sentences.zh: 他用一块木头把身后的外门卡死。

sentences.en: And then he puts his eye to a peephole into Lincoln's box.
sentences.zh: 然后他把眼睛凑到通往林肯包厢的窥视孔上。

sentences.en: Now, it's often said that he had bored the peephole earlier that day.
sentences.zh: 现在，人们常说他在那天早些时候钻了这个窥视孔。

sentences.en: In fact, there was a very, very detailed and actually brilliant book on John Wilkes Booth by Michael Kaufman called American Brutus.
sentences.zh: 事实上，迈克尔·考夫曼写过一本非常非常详细且实际上很精彩的关于约翰·威尔克斯·布斯的书，名为《美国布鲁图斯》。

sentences.en: One for you, Tom.
sentences.zh: 这本书适合你读，汤姆。

sentences.en: And in that book, Kaufman quotes the son of the theatre manager, Harry Ford, who wrote in
sentences.zh: 在那本书中，考夫曼引用了剧院经理哈里·福特的儿子的写于

sentences.en: 1962 that Booth had nothing to do with this peephole.
sentences.zh: 1962年的话，称布斯与这个窥视孔毫无关系。

sentences.en: It was always there that the theatre manager had bored it himself so that bodyguards, if they were there, could see into the presidential box and that Lincoln's entourage could see
sentences.zh: 那个洞一直是开着的，剧院经理自己把它凿出来的，好让保镖（如果当时有保镖的话）能看到总统包厢里面，也让林肯的随从能看到

sentences.en: what he was up to.
sentences.zh: 他在搞什么鬼。

sentences.en: Anyway, Booth looks through this hole and you can see there are four people in the box.
sentences.zh: 总之，布斯通过这个洞望过去，你可以看到包厢里有四个人。

sentences.en: There's Lincoln in the rocking chair.
sentences.zh: 林肯正坐在摇椅里。

sentences.en: There's Mary.
sentences.zh: 玛丽也在。

sentences.en: There's Clara Harris.
sentences.zh: 克拉拉·哈里斯也在。

sentences.en: There's Major Rathbone on this sofa.
sentences.zh: 雷斯本少校正坐在那张沙发上。

sentences.en: And now Booth waits.
sentences.zh: 现在布斯在等待。

sentences.en: He doesn't go in.
sentences.zh: 他没有进去。

sentences.en: He's thought about this quite carefully.
sentences.zh: 他对此考虑得相当周全。

sentences.en: He has an escape plan.
sentences.zh: 他有一套逃跑计划。

sentences.en: He knows the moment he wants to strike.
sentences.zh: 他知道自己想在哪个时刻动手。

sentences.en: Because he's an actor, he knows this play very well.
sentences.zh: 因为他是个演员，他对这部戏非常熟悉。

sentences.en: He knows there will be a perfect moment when there's going to be a great punchline.
sentences.zh: 他知道会有一个完美的时机，会有一个绝佳的俏皮话。

sentences.en: The stage will be almost deserted.
sentences.zh: 舞台上几乎空无一人。

sentences.en: Everybody will be laughing and he can make his move.
sentences.zh: 所有人都将在大笑，而他可以趁机行动。

sentences.en: And this is the hilarious stretch of dialogue that you rendered in the previous episode.
sentences.zh: 这就是你在上一集里呈现的那段极其搞笑的台词。

sentences.en: But it's so funny that I think we should hear it again.
sentences.zh: 但它太搞笑了，我觉得我们应该再听一遍。

sentences.en: Oh, wonderful.
sentences.zh: 噢，太棒了。

sentences.en: So it's 10.15.
sentences.zh: 所以现在是10点15分。

sentences.en: We're at Act 3, Scene 2.
sentences.zh: 我们正处在第三幕第二场。

sentences.en: And Harry Hawke, maybe Tom, you'd like to do Harry Hawke and I'll play Mrs. Mount Chessington.
sentences.zh: 哈里·霍克，也许汤姆，你想来演哈里·霍克，我来演蒙特切辛顿夫人。

sentences.en: So Harry Hawke is playing the American Cousin and he's arguing with this woman called Mrs.
sentences.zh: 哈里·霍克饰演这位美国表亲，他正在和一位名叫蒙特切辛顿夫人的女士争吵

sentences.en: Mount Chessington, so Lady Bracknell figure.
sentences.zh: 也就是布拉克内尔夫人那样的人物。

sentences.en: And she storms off the stage and she says, I am aware, Mr. Trenchard.
sentences.zh: 然后她气冲冲地跑下台，说道：“我知道，特伦查德先生。

sentences.en: You are not used to the manners of good society.
sentences.zh: 你还不习惯上流社会的礼仪。”

sentences.en: Don't know the manners of good society, eh?
sentences.zh: 不懂上流社会的礼仪，是吧？

sentences.en: Well, I guess you know enough to turn you inside out, old gal.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我想你足够懂，能让你脱胎换骨呢，老太婆。

sentences.en: You so-to-logising old man-trap, you.
sentences.zh: 你这个满嘴大道理的老夹子。

sentences.en: And everybody roars with laughter at this absolutely tremendous repartee.
sentences.zh: 每个人都对这绝对精彩的唇枪舌剑爆发出雷鸣般的笑声。

sentences.en: As they would.
sentences.zh: 本该如此。

sentences.en: And it is at that moment, Tom, that John Wilkes Booth, he opens the door of the box.
sentences.zh: 就在那个时刻，汤姆，约翰·威克斯·布斯打开了包厢的门。

sentences.en: He takes out a Derringer pistol from his pocket.
sentences.zh: 他从口袋里掏出一把德林杰手枪。

sentences.en: He takes a single step towards Abraham Lincoln's rocking chair.
sentences.zh: 他朝着亚伯拉罕·林肯的摇椅迈出了一步。

sentences.en: He levels it at the back of Lincoln's head.
sentences.zh: 他把枪对准了林肯的后脑勺。

sentences.en: And he fires.
sentences.zh: 然后他开枪了。

sentences.en: Point blank range.
sentences.zh: 零距离射击。

sentences.en: Point blank range.
sentences.zh: 零距离射击。

sentences.en: Now, as soon as the shot rings out, Major Rathbone leaps to his feet.
sentences.zh: 枪声一响，雷斯本少校立刻跳了起来。

sentences.en: He suddenly realises what's happening.
sentences.zh: 他突然意识到发生了什么。

sentences.en: There's a dark figure in the box.
sentences.zh: 包厢里有一个黑影。

sentences.en: He lunges towards the figure.
sentences.zh: 他向那个黑影猛扑过去。

sentences.en: And then he shrinks back because he sees the glint of a knife in Booth's other hand.
sentences.zh: 接着他又畏缩了，因为他看到布斯的另一只手里闪烁着刀光。

sentences.en: And Booth is fired with one hand.
sentences.zh: 布斯用一只手开枪。

sentences.en: And then with the other hand, he strikes with the dagger into Rathbone's arm.
sentences.zh: 然后用另一只手用匕首刺向雷斯本的手臂。

sentences.en: And he slices through his arm.
sentences.zh: 他划破了他的手臂。

sentences.en: Rathbone falls backwards towards the sofa.
sentences.zh: 雷斯本向后倒向沙发。

sentences.en: This is all in a second.
sentences.zh: 这一切都发生在短短一秒钟内。

sentences.en: The two women are so stunned.
sentences.zh: 两个女人震惊得说不出话来。

sentences.en: They're obviously deafened by the shot and just amazed.
sentences.zh: 她们显然被枪声震得耳鸣，而且惊呆了。

sentences.en: They have not really reacted.
sentences.zh: 她们还没来得及真正反应过来。

sentences.en: So this is when Booth pulls off the really sort of remarkable bit of his plan.
sentences.zh: 所以，就在这时，布斯完成了他计划中最惊人的一部分。

sentences.en: He strides past them to the rail of the box.
sentences.zh: 他大步从她们身边走过，来到包厢的栏杆前。

sentences.en: He puts one hand on the rail and then he vaults over the rail down 12 feet and lands on the stage.
sentences.zh: 他把一只手放在栏杆上，然后越过栏杆纵身一跃，跳下12英尺，落在了舞台上。

sentences.en: Now, it's often said that he caught a spur in his boot on one of the flags decorating the box.
sentences.zh: 人们常说，他在跳下时，靴子上的马刺挂在了装饰包厢的一面旗帜上。

sentences.en: Actually, only one witness.
sentences.zh: 事实上，只有一个目击者。

sentences.en: This bloke that I mentioned earlier with the opera glasses, James Ferguson.
sentences.zh: 就是我刚才提到的那个拿着歌剧望远镜的家伙，詹姆斯·弗格森。

sentences.en: He's the only person who said he saw this happen.
sentences.zh: 他是唯一一个说自己看到这一幕的人。

sentences.en: Nobody else said they saw it.
sentences.zh: 没有其他人说他们看到了。

sentences.en: Has he hurt himself at all?
sentences.zh: 他受伤了吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So he definitely does.
sentences.zh: 所以他确实受伤了。

sentences.en: Some accounts say because he did this, caught his spur, he then fell very awkwardly onto the stage.
sentences.zh: 有些记述说，因为他挂住了马刺，所以落地时姿势非常尴尬。

sentences.en: I think if you'd caught your spur, you'd fall much more awkwardly than he falls.
sentences.zh: 我想如果你挂住了马刺，摔下来肯定会比他现在更难看。

sentences.en: I think he falls.
sentences.zh: 我认为他摔了。

sentences.en: He lands slightly awkwardly.
sentences.zh: 他落地时姿势稍微有点别扭。

sentences.en: It's quite a big drop.
sentences.zh: 那是一个相当高的落差。

sentences.en: And he effectively fractures his leg, as we will discover.
sentences.zh: 正如我们后来发现的那样，他实际上骨折了。

sentences.en: But the interesting thing is at this point, there are many, many accounts of what happened from witnesses at the time.
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，对于当时现场目击者所发生的事，有非常非常多的记述。

sentences.en: None of them tell the same thing.
sentences.zh: 没有一份记述是完全相同的。

sentences.en: So for people who listen to our JFK series, who were struck by the discrepancies in the eyewitness accounts, this is exactly the same thing as it is so often in history.
sentences.zh: 所以，对于听过我们肯尼迪系列节目、对目击者证词中的出入感到震惊的人来说，这和历史上的情况如出一辙。

sentences.en: There's nothing unique about the Kennedy murder.
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪遇刺案并没有什么特殊之处。

sentences.en: People didn't even agree on what Booth said.
sentences.zh: 人们甚至对布斯说了什么都意见不一。

sentences.en: Harry Hawke, the actor, who was just about to walk off stage, he was convinced that as Booth was preparing to jump, he shouted the word,
sentences.zh: 演员哈里·霍克当时正准备下台，他确信布斯在准备跳下时大喊了一句：

sentences.en: Sick Semper Tyrannus, Hawke said, then he jumped onto the stage, he straightened up, he raised his dagger over his head, and he shouted, the South shall be free.
sentences.zh: 霍克说，喊的是“暴君永世不得好下场”，接着他跳到舞台上，直起身子，把匕首举过头顶，大喊：“南方必将获得自由。”

sentences.en: But other witnesses said, no, that's not right at all.
sentences.zh: 但其他目击者说，不对，根本不是这样的。

sentences.en: He only shouted, Sick Semper Tyrannus, so always to tyrants.
sentences.zh: 他一落到舞台上，只喊了“暴君永世不得好下场”。

sentences.en: Once he'd landed on the stage.
sentences.zh: 一旦他落到舞台上。

sentences.en: And other people said, well, he didn't say that at all.
sentences.zh: 还有人说，噢，他根本没说那个。

sentences.en: He said the South should be avenged.
sentences.zh: 他说的是“南方应当复仇”。

sentences.en: Or some people just said, he said, I've done it, and then ran off the stage.
sentences.zh: 或者有些人干脆说，他喊了句“我做到了”，然后就逃跑了。

sentences.en: So, you know, if you read a definitive account, you know, you paid your money and takes your choice, really.
sentences.zh: 所以你知道的，如果你去读一份权威的记述，这就全看你信哪一个了。

sentences.en: There's no reason to trust one version rather than another.
sentences.zh: 没有理由去相信某个版本而否定另一个版本。

sentences.en: I suppose the one big difference with the Kennedy assassination is that if he shot Lincoln at point blank range,
sentences.zh: 我想肯尼迪刺杀案最大的不同在于，如果他是近距离枪击林肯的话，

sentences.en: there's no question about who did it and where the bullet came from.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问是谁干的以及子弹是从哪儿射出来的。

sentences.en: Exactly not at all.
sentences.zh: 一点也没错。

sentences.en: The only thing that everybody agrees, everyone really agrees, is that once he's landed on the stage and said whatever he said, he turned, he ran into the wings, into the darkness,
sentences.zh: 唯一所有人意见一致、真正达成共识的是，一旦他落到舞台上并说完了那些话，他就转身跑进了侧台的黑暗中，

sentences.en: and he vanished from sight.
sentences.zh: 消失得无影无踪。

sentences.en: So he ran, but he's fractured his leg, perhaps, or?
sentences.zh: 所以他跑了，但他可能骨折了，还是怎么的？

sentences.en: So he's fired by adrenaline, or?
sentences.zh: 所以他是靠肾上腺素支撑，还是怎么的？

sentences.en: Fired by adrenaline, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想是靠肾上腺素支撑。

sentences.en: Because as you'll find out, he doesn't just run, he then rides for hours.
sentences.zh: 因为正如你将发现的，他不仅是逃跑，接下来他还骑了几个小时的马。

sentences.en: So we'll pick up on John Wilkes Booth's story in the second half, but for now, let's stay in the theatre.
sentences.zh: 我们将在下半场继续讲述约翰·威克斯·布斯的故事，但现在，让我们留在剧院里。

sentences.en: Most people's reaction is total shock and confusion.
sentences.zh: 大多数人的反应是极度的震惊和混乱。

sentences.en: Now, at first, most people thought it was part of the play, or they thought it was a slightly tasteless stunt to mark Abraham Lincoln's presence.
sentences.zh: 起初，大多数人以为那是戏剧的一部分，或者他们以为那是为了庆祝亚伯拉罕·林肯到场而搞的一个略显低俗的恶作剧。

sentences.en: Or a lot of people actually said, I thought something had fallen over at the back.
sentences.zh: 或者很多人其实在说：“我以为是后面有什么东西倒了。”

sentences.en: I heard a big bang, and I thought something had fallen over in the auditorium, had a bit of the stage fallen over.
sentences.zh: “我听到一声巨响，我以为是观众席里有什么东西倒了，或者是舞台的一部分塌了。”

sentences.en: You know, who knows what it was.
sentences.zh: 谁知道当时到底是什么呢。

sentences.en: The theatre staff, who have been half-watching through kind of windows and things, they were stunned when they saw Booth, of all people on stage.
sentences.zh: 剧院的工作人员之前一直透过各种窗户半信半疑地看着，当他们看到布斯竟然出现在舞台上时，全都惊呆了。

sentences.en: One of them actually burst out.
sentences.zh: 其中一个人甚至脱口而出。

sentences.en: He said, by God, is John Booth crazy?
sentences.zh: 他说：“天哪，约翰·布斯疯了吗？”

sentences.en: So it's kind of like Brad Pitt suddenly appearing on the stage and waving a gun.
sentences.zh: 所以这有点像布拉德·皮特突然出现在舞台上挥舞着一把枪。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 一点没错。

sentences.en: Now, then they heard people screaming from the president's box.
sentences.zh: 接着他们听到总统包厢里传出了尖叫声。

sentences.en: When people hear screaming, then they panic, and people start to run, so there's a bit of a stampede.
sentences.zh: 当人们听到尖叫声时，就会陷入恐慌，开始逃跑，于是便发生了踩踏事故。

sentences.en: Some people are charging onto the stage, trying to get onto the stage after John Wilkes Booth.
sentences.zh: 有些人冲上舞台，试图追着约翰·威克斯·布斯上台。

sentences.en: Some people are just running out of the theatre because they think there's a general attack.
sentences.zh: 有些人只是夺门逃出剧院，因为他们以为遭到了全面袭击。

sentences.en: Other people trying to get into Lincoln's box.
sentences.zh: 还有人试图进入林肯的包厢。

sentences.en: In the box, Mary Lincoln is bent over her husband.
sentences.zh: 在包厢里，玛丽·林肯正俯身在丈夫身上。

sentences.en: She's sobbing.
sentences.zh: 她在啜泣。

sentences.en: She's saying, talk to me, talk to me, all this, because he's slumped in his chair.
sentences.zh: 她说：“跟我说话，跟我说话，”诸如此类的话，因为他已经瘫软在椅子里了。

sentences.en: Are you going to say something horrid about her now, or are you going to feel a measure of pity for this poor woman?
sentences.zh: 你现在是要说一些关于她的刻薄话，还是打算对这个可怜的女人产生一丝同情？

sentences.en: No, I feel sorry for her.
sentences.zh: 不，我挺替她难过的。

sentences.en: I feel sorry for her.
sentences.zh: 我挺同情她的。

sentences.en: She's not really well-treated, actually, as Lincoln is dying, as we shall see.
sentences.zh: 事实上，正如我们所见，在林肯垂死之际，她并没有受到很好的对待。

sentences.en: You feel sorry for her, don't you, Tom?
sentences.zh: 你也替她难过对吧，汤姆？

sentences.en: I do, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我是，对的。

sentences.en: Lovely.
sentences.zh: 很好。

sentences.en: Reflects very well on you.
sentences.zh: 这很能体现你的品德。

sentences.en: Major Rathbone is in shock.
sentences.zh: 雷斯本少校处于休克状态。

sentences.en: He's had his arm chopped off, hasn't he, basically.
sentences.zh: 他的手臂基本上可以说是被砍断了，对吧。

sentences.en: It's a big slice down his arm, and there's blood soaking into his sleeve.
sentences.zh: 他的手臂上有一道大大的伤口，鲜血浸透了他的袖子。

sentences.en: Now, even though he's losing a lot of blood, he has the presence of mind to try and open the door of the box, and he realises that Booth has jammed it.
sentences.zh: 现在，尽管他失血过多，他依然保持着清醒的头脑，试图打开包厢的门，但他发现布斯把门给卡死了。

sentences.en: So there are other people hammering on the door, so between them, they manage to get the door open, and people burst into the box.
sentences.zh: 于是其他人开始砸门，他们齐心协力终于把门打开了，人们涌进了包厢。

sentences.en: Now, one of them is a young doctor who's only been qualified for a few weeks, I think, called Charles Leal.
sentences.zh: 其中有一个年轻医生，我想他拿到行医资格才几个星期，名叫查尔斯·利尔。

sentences.en: He's in his 20s, and he's joined by an older doctor from the army, a Signal Corps surgeon called Charles Taft.
sentences.zh: 他二十多岁，和他一起来的是一位来自军队的老军医，一名通信兵外科医生，名叫查尔斯·塔夫特。

sentences.en: Leal, the younger man, is the first to Lincoln's body, and he finds the president.
sentences.zh: 年轻的利尔第一个来到林肯身边，他发现了总统。

sentences.en: He's comatose.
sentences.zh: 他处于昏迷状态。

sentences.en: He's unconscious.
sentences.zh: 他失去了知觉。

sentences.en: He's breathing, very laboured breathing.
sentences.zh: 他在呼吸，呼吸非常艰难。

sentences.en: And interestingly, although it's point-bank range, Leal can't actually find the wound at first, because it's only a small pistol.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，尽管是近距离射击，但利尔起初居然找不到伤口，因为这只是一把小手枪。

sentences.en: And at first, because everybody had seen Booth lifting, waving this bloody knife on stage, they assume that Lincoln has been stabbed.
sentences.zh: 而且起初，由于大家都看到布斯在舞台上举着、挥舞着这把带血的匕首，他们以为林肯是被刺伤的。

sentences.en: And it's interesting, that, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这很有趣，对吧？

sentences.en: I'd never thought that.
sentences.zh: 我以前从没想过这一点。

sentences.en: But of course, Caesar had been murdered with a dagger.
sentences.zh: 但当然，凯撒是被匕首谋杀的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So for a Shakespeare actor to stand on a stage and wave a dagger is much more natural than for him, say, to wave a gun.
sentences.zh: 所以对于一个莎士比亚演员来说，站在舞台上挥舞匕首要比挥舞一把枪自然得多。

sentences.en: Yeah, I guess so.
sentences.zh: 对，我想是的。

sentences.en: I guess so.
sentences.zh: 我想也是。

sentences.en: I hadn't thought that, actually, that that's the thing that he waves.
sentences.zh: 我之前确实没想过，原来他挥舞的是这个。

sentences.en: The semiotics of it is much more Shakespearean.
sentences.zh: 这里的符号学意义要莎士比亚得多。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 一点没错。

sentences.en: It is much more classical.
sentences.zh: 这要古典得多。

sentences.en: So with some soldiers, Leal gets Lincoln to the floor.
sentences.zh: 所以在几名士兵的协助下，利尔把林肯放倒在地上。

sentences.en: They still can't find the wound.
sentences.zh: 他们仍然找不到伤口。

sentences.en: They're cutting off his shirt, assuming he's been stabbed.
sentences.zh: 他们剪开他的衬衫，以为他被刺伤了。

sentences.en: And then Leal runs his hand through Lincoln's hair, and he finds a bullet hole at the back of his head.
sentences.zh: 接着利尔把手伸进林肯的头发里，在林肯的后脑勺发现了一个弹孔。

sentences.en: A small bullet hole with a swelling around it.
sentences.zh: 一个小小的弹孔，周围有些肿胀。

sentences.en: And the blood's already started to clot.
sentences.zh: 而且血已经开始凝固了。

sentences.en: And as Leal ruffles through Lincoln's hair, the clot opens up.
sentences.zh: 当利尔拨弄林肯的头发时，血块裂开了。

sentences.en: And blood pours out.
sentences.zh: 鲜血喷涌而出。

sentences.en: But at that point, Lincoln starts to breathe more easily.
sentences.zh: 但就在那时，林肯的呼吸开始变得顺畅。

sentences.en: Now, at this point, the soldiers are already saying, we've got to get the president back to the White House.
sentences.zh: 这时候，士兵们已经在说，我们必须把总统送回白宫。

sentences.en: And the surgeon, the army surgeon, Dr. Taft, steps in.
sentences.zh: 而外科医生，陆军外科医生塔夫特博士介入了。

sentences.en: He says, listen, I know what I'm talking about.
sentences.zh: 他说，听着，我知道自己在说什么。

sentences.en: We cannot take him there.
sentences.zh: 我们不能把他带到那里去。

sentences.en: You can't move him a long way.
sentences.zh: 你不能把他运送太远。

sentences.en: Where we should take him is the nearest house.
sentences.zh: 我们应该把他带到最近的房子里。

sentences.en: And they want to do this because they feel it would be vulgar for a president to die in a theatre.
sentences.zh: 他们之所以想这么做，是因为觉得让总统死在剧院里太有失体面了。

sentences.en: They already know he's basically dead.
sentences.zh: 他们已经知道他基本上没救了。

sentences.en: This is so interesting.
sentences.zh: 这太有趣了。

sentences.en: This is Michael Kaufman's theory.
sentences.zh: 这是迈克尔·考夫曼的理论。

sentences.en: Because Kaufman points out, at this point, just to be clear, both of these doctors are in no doubt whatsoever that Lincoln is a dead man.
sentences.zh: 因为考夫曼指出，在此，需要明确的是，这两位医生都毫不怀疑林肯已经是个死人了。

sentences.en: There is no way, if you've been shot in the back of the head, a point blank range that you will possibly survive.
sentences.zh: 如果你在极近的距离被子弹击中后脑勺，你绝无生还的可能。

sentences.en: So they know he's dying, but they don't want him to die on Good Friday in a playhouse.
sentences.zh: 所以他们知道他快死了，但他们不想让他在耶稣受难日死在戏院里。

sentences.en: It's so indecorous.
sentences.zh: 这太不得体了。

sentences.en: Indecorous is the word, yeah.
sentences.zh: “不得体”就是这个词，没错。

sentences.en: So they organise a bearer party and they take Lincoln out of the box, down the stairs, through the sort of foyer and across the road to the nearest house, which is a lodging house,
sentences.zh: 于是他们组织了一支担架队，把林肯从包厢抬出来，走下楼梯，穿过门厅，来到马路对面的最近的房子，那是一栋寄宿公寓，

sentences.en: ironically, obviously because it's close to the theatre, very popular with actors, run by a German tailor called William Peterson.
sentences.zh: 具有讽刺意味的是，显然因为它离剧院很近，深受演员欢迎，由一个叫威廉·彼得森的德国裁缝经营。

sentences.en: And they take him to a back bedroom on the ground floor.
sentences.zh: 他们把他抬到了底楼的一间后卧室。

sentences.en: And Lincoln is such a long man, a very tall man, that he won't fit on a bed, so they have to lie him kind of diagonally across the bed.
sentences.zh: 林肯个子太高了，是个身材极其高大的人，床根本装不下他，所以他们只好让他斜躺在床上。

sentences.en: Now, Mary Lincoln kind of trails behind them.
sentences.zh: 此时，玛丽·林肯跌跌撞撞地跟在他们后面。

sentences.en: She's in a total daze, not surprisingly, in a state of shock.
sentences.zh: 她整个人处于完全茫然的状态，毫不奇怪，处于休克状态。

sentences.en: So are Clara Harris and this poor bloke, Major Rathbone, who basically comes very close to death because Booth had actually severed an artery.
sentences.zh: 克拉拉·哈里斯和这个可怜的家伙——雷斯本少校也是如此，他差点丧命，因为布思实际上割断了他的一条动脉。

sentences.en: And has his arm been patched up by this point?
sentences.zh: 此时他的胳膊已经包扎好了吗？

sentences.en: His arm is eventually patched up.
sentences.zh: 他的胳膊最终包扎好了。

sentences.en: But actually, Mary Lincoln could never look at Clara and Major Rathbone again, I think.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，我想玛丽·林肯再也无法面对克拉拉和雷斯本少校了。

sentences.en: She associated them with that knight.
sentences.zh: 她把他们与那个夜晚联系在了一起。

sentences.en: Anyway, the soldiers eventually get Mary Lincoln across the street.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，士兵们最终把玛丽·林肯护送过了街。

sentences.en: And for a time, she just stands on her own in the front parlour, kind of just standing in shock.
sentences.zh: 有一段时间，她独自站在前客厅里，处于震惊之中，茫然地站着。

sentences.en: I feel really sorry for her.
sentences.zh: 我真的很为她感到难过。

sentences.en: She's lost her son.
sentences.zh: 她失去了儿子。

sentences.en: Now she's lost her husband.
sentences.zh: 现在她又失去了丈夫。

sentences.en: And all you can do is moan about the fact that she's occasionally a little bit sniffy about very attractive women riding with her husband.
sentences.zh: 而你却只能抱怨她偶尔对那些和她丈夫骑马的迷人女性有点挑剔。

sentences.en: I'm totally team Mrs. Lincoln.
sentences.zh: 我百分之百支持林肯夫人。

sentences.en: I moaned in the last episode, but not in this one.
sentences.zh: 我在上一集抱怨过，但这一集没有。

sentences.en: She goes down the hall to her husband.
sentences.zh: 她穿过走廊去看望她的丈夫。

sentences.en: People describe her sobbing in, in quote, extreme anguish.
sentences.zh: 人们形容她在“极度痛苦”中啜泣。

sentences.en: There's blood and brain tissue slowly leaking out of his head, but she's kissing his head nonetheless.
sentences.zh: 鲜血和脑组织正从他的头部缓缓渗出，但她还是吻了他的头部。

sentences.en: And she's begging him to speak.
sentences.zh: 她恳求他说说话。

sentences.en: Now at this point, tons of people have crowded into the room.
sentences.zh: 此时，无数的人涌入了房间。

sentences.en: Above all, the Secretary of War, Edwin Stanton, who takes charge.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是战争部长埃德温·斯坦顿，他接管了局面。

sentences.en: They all are very clear at this point that Lincoln will die.
sentences.zh: 他们此时都非常清楚林肯将要离世。

sentences.en: They call for his son, Robert, who's 21, his oldest son.
sentences.zh: 他们叫来了他的大儿子罗伯特，他21岁。

sentences.en: He's been serving on General Grant's staff as an army captain.
sentences.zh: 他一直在格兰特将军的参谋部担任陆军上尉。

sentences.en: He breaks down, but he feels he has to sort of present a stoical, you know, he mans up as it were.
sentences.zh: 他崩溃了，但他觉得必须表现得坚强，你知道的，他必须像个真正的男子汉。

sentences.en: He's now the head of the house.
sentences.zh: 他现在是家里的顶梁柱了。

sentences.en: Head of the house.
sentences.zh: 家里的顶梁柱。

sentences.en: And he composes himself.
sentences.zh: 他镇定下来。

sentences.en: And he actually says, I want to get one of my mother's friends, who's a senator's wife called Elizabeth Dixon, to come over here and to calm my mother down.
sentences.zh: 他实际上说，我想找我母亲的一个朋友，一位名叫伊丽莎白·迪克森的参议员妻子过来，好让我母亲平静下来。

sentences.en: But Mary keeps kind of bursting back into the room and begging her husband to wake up and live for the sake of the children, which is actually what Franz Ferdinand said to Sophie,
sentences.zh: 但玛丽不断地冲回房间，恳求她的丈夫醒来，为了孩子们的缘故活下去，这实际上就是弗朗茨·斐迪南对索菲说过的话，

sentences.en: if you remember, when they were dying in Sarajevo.
sentences.zh: 如果你还记得的话，当他们在萨拉热窝垂死之际。

sentences.en: Now we have the doctor's notes, one of the doctor's notes.
sentences.zh: 现在我们有了医生的记录，其中一位医生的记录。

sentences.en: He made quite detailed notes of Lincoln's sort of decline across the night.
sentences.zh: 他相当详细地记录了林肯在这一夜间病情恶化的过程。

sentences.en: He was very quiet.
sentences.zh: 他非常安静。

sentences.en: He's just, he's unconscious, breathing with great difficulty.
sentences.zh: 他只是，他昏迷不醒，呼吸异常艰难。

sentences.en: They're really just all waiting for the end.
sentences.zh: 大家其实都只是在等待最后的时刻。

sentences.en: They called for a chaplain from the Senate, the Senate chaplain, who's called Dr. Gurley.
sentences.zh: 他们找来了一位参议院的牧师，即参议院牧师格利博士。

sentences.en: And he said his last prayers at half past three.
sentences.zh: 他在三点半作了最后一次祈祷。

sentences.en: But Lincoln lived for another three hours or so.
sentences.zh: 但林肯又活了大约三个小时。

sentences.en: At seven o'clock in the morning, his breathing became very ragged and they all knew the end was near.
sentences.zh: 清晨七点，他的呼吸变得非常急促，大家都知道大限已至。

sentences.en: And at that point, Mary came back in.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，玛丽又进来了。

sentences.en: She realized he was about to die.
sentences.zh: 她意识到他快要死了。

sentences.en: And she had a kind of shrieking fit and threw herself onto the ground.
sentences.zh: 她发出一阵尖叫，扑倒在地上。

sentences.en: And Edwin Stanton, who does not share your view, I think it's fair to say, Mrs. Lincoln, he went ballistic and he shouted, take that woman out and do not let her in here again.
sentences.zh: 而埃德温·斯坦顿，我觉得公平地说，他并不赞同你对林肯夫人的看法，他勃然大怒并大喊道，把那个女人带出去，不准她再进来。

sentences.en: Oh, right.
sentences.zh: 哦，这样啊。

sentences.en: So his approach to the grieving widow is very much yours.
sentences.zh: 所以他对这位悲伤遗孀的处理方式简直和你如出一辙。

sentences.en: I've never been in that circumstance with a grieving widow, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我可从未在那种情况下面对过悲伤的遗孀。

sentences.en: I mean, I mean, I hope for the sake of a grieving widow that you're not.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，为了悲伤遗孀好，我希望你也没有。

sentences.en: Mrs. Dixon took Mary out.
sentences.zh: 迪克森夫人把玛丽带了出去。

sentences.en: Mary is sobbing very loudly and actually blaming herself.
sentences.zh: 玛丽哭得撕心裂肺，甚至开始责怪自己。

sentences.en: She says, oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 她说，天哪。

sentences.en: And have I given my husband to die?
sentences.zh: 难道是我害死了我的丈夫吗？

sentences.en: Because, of course, she persuaded him to go to the theater.
sentences.zh: 因为，当然是她劝他去剧院的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: It's a tragic story.
sentences.zh: 这是一个悲惨的故事。

sentences.en: And then that's the end.
sentences.zh: 然后就结束了。

sentences.en: And Edwin Stanton, with properly Hollywood flair, just says, now he belongs to the ages.
sentences.zh: 而埃德温·斯坦顿带着恰到好处的好莱坞风范说，他现在属于永恒了。

sentences.en: So obviously rehearsed.
sentences.zh: 显然是彩排过的。

sentences.en: Captain, my captain.
sentences.zh: 我的船长，我的船长。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Mary's out of the room at this point.
sentences.zh: 此时玛丽已经离开了房间。

sentences.en: The chaplain goes into the parlor to tell Mary the news.
sentences.zh: 牧师走进客厅把这个消息告诉了玛丽。

sentences.en: And she shrieks at him.
sentences.zh: 而她对他尖叫。

sentences.en: She says, why didn't you let me know that he was dying?
sentences.zh: 她说，他快死了，你为什么不通知我？

sentences.en: Why didn't you tell me?
sentences.zh: 你为什么不告诉我？

sentences.en: Gurley says to her, your friends thought it wasn't beSt.
sentences.zh: 格利对她说，你的朋友们认为这样最好。

sentences.en: You must be resigned to the will of God.
sentences.zh: 你必须顺从上帝的旨意。

sentences.en: You must be calm and trust in your God and in your friends.
sentences.zh: 你必须保持冷静，信仰你的上帝和朋友。

sentences.en: Now, Tom, you feel very sorry for Mary.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你对玛丽深表同情。

sentences.en: But I have to say, after this, she slightly disgraces herself.
sentences.zh: 但我必须说，在这之后，她有点自取其辱。

sentences.en: Because when she moves out of the White House, she steals 70 packing cases worth of stuff.
sentences.zh: 因为当她搬出白宫时，她偷了整整70箱的东西。

sentences.en: She steals the silver, the spoons, the carpets and the curtains.
sentences.zh: 她偷了银器、勺子、地毯和窗帘。

sentences.en: She is, in fact, the Lobelia Sackville Baggins of American history.
sentences.zh: 她实际上就是美国历史上的洛贝莉亚·萨克维尔-巴金斯。

sentences.en: I think that's harsh.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这太苛刻了。

sentences.en: I actually looked up.
sentences.zh: 我其实查阅过。

sentences.en: Lobelia Sackville Baggins.
sentences.zh: 洛贝莉亚·萨克维尔-巴金斯。

sentences.en: No, go on.
sentences.zh: 不，你说下去。

sentences.en: No, no.
sentences.zh: 不，不。

sentences.en: About Mrs Lincoln in the Bodleian.
sentences.zh: 关于博德利图书馆里的林肯夫人。

sentences.en: And I read that she wore mourning for the rest of her life, like Queen Victoria.
sentences.zh: 我读到她像维多利亚女王一样，余生都在为丈夫服丧。

sentences.en: And Queen Victoria wrote a very sympathetic letter to her.
sentences.zh: 维多利亚女王还给她写了一封非常同情的信。

sentences.en: And I think it reflects well on Queen Victoria that she was sympathetic, unlike you, who has compared her to one of the less appealing figures from Lord of the Rings.
sentences.zh: 我认为维多利亚女王表现得很有同情心，这为她增色不少，不像你，把她比作《指环王》里不那么讨喜的角色之一。

sentences.en: And I think listeners will draw their own conclusions from this.
sentences.zh: 我想听众们会从中得出自己的结论。

sentences.en: Queen Victoria would have changed the tune if she'd found out that stuff about the silver.
sentences.zh: 如果维多利亚女王发现银器的事，她就会改变调子了。

sentences.en: If she'd known about the flipping spoons, she'd have changed her mind.
sentences.zh: 如果她知道那些该死的勺子，她就会改变主意了。

sentences.en: I don't think so.
sentences.zh: 我不这么认为。

sentences.en: For me, you say she's the real victim.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，你说她是真正的受害者。

sentences.en: For me, the saddest part is actually Tad or Taddy, their son.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，最令人伤心的其实是塔德或塔迪，他们的儿子。

sentences.en: Taddy was 12.
sentences.zh: 塔迪当时12岁。

sentences.en: We talked about him in the last episode.
sentences.zh: 我们在上一集聊过他。

sentences.en: He had a cleft palate, very serious problems with his speech.
sentences.zh: 他有腭裂，说话有很严重的障碍。

sentences.en: So he's had a kind of rough deal, generally.
sentences.zh: 所以总的来说，他的命运挺坎坷的。

sentences.en: He's only recently celebrated his 12th birthday.
sentences.zh: 他不久前才刚庆祝完12岁生日。

sentences.en: And he didn't come with them to the play, because it's a very boring play for a 12-year-old.
sentences.zh: 他没有和他们一起去看戏，因为对一个12岁的孩子来说，那场戏太无聊了。

sentences.en: His tutor had taken him to another theatre to see Aladdin.
sentences.zh: 他的家庭教师带他去了另一家剧院看《阿拉丁》。

sentences.en: And at one point, Mary said, oh, let's send for Taddy, because his father loves Taddy so much, he will wake up when he hears Taddy's voice.
sentences.zh: 有一次玛丽说，哦，派人把塔迪叫来吧，因为他父亲太爱塔迪了，一听到塔迪的声音他就会醒过来的。

sentences.en: But then she thought better of it.
sentences.zh: 但转念一想，她又觉得不妥。

sentences.en: Oh, no, poor Taddy.
sentences.zh: 哦，不，可怜的塔迪。

sentences.en: You know, he'll be too upset.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他会伤心欲绝的。

sentences.en: Now, Taddy, it's a terrible scene.
sentences.zh: 现在，塔迪，那场面太可怕了。

sentences.en: He's at Aladdin when the theatre managers stop the play and announce that the president has been shot.
sentences.zh: 他正在看《阿拉丁》，这时剧院经理叫停了演出，宣布总统遭到枪击。

sentences.en: I mean, imagine being Taddy.
sentences.zh: 我是说，想象一下塔迪当时的感受。

sentences.en: He is hysterical, of course, and he's taken back to the White House in floods of tears.
sentences.zh: 当然，他歇斯底里，泪流满面地被送回了白宫。

sentences.en: He seems to have convinced himself overnight that his father would live.
sentences.zh: 一夜之间，他似乎已经确信自己的父亲会活下来。

sentences.en: So when people start returning to the house the next day, he's saying, where's my pa?
sentences.zh: 所以当人们第二天开始回到屋里时，他在说，我的爸爸呢？

sentences.en: Where's my pa?
sentences.zh: 我的爸爸呢？

sentences.en: And the chaplain, Reverend Gurley, says, Taddy, your pa is dead.
sentences.zh: 牧师格利神父说，塔迪，你的爸爸死了。

sentences.en: And Taddy breaks down.
sentences.zh: 塔迪情绪崩溃。

sentences.en: Oh, my father is dead.
sentences.zh: 哦，我的父亲死了。

sentences.en: What shall I do?
sentences.zh: 我该怎么办？

sentences.en: Oh, he says he's begging his mother, don't die, Ma.
sentences.zh: 哦，听说他哀求母亲，妈妈，别死。

sentences.en: Don't die.
sentences.zh: 别死。

sentences.en: I'll be left alone.
sentences.zh: 我会孤单一个人的。

sentences.en: I'll be left alone.
sentences.zh: 我会孤单一个人的。

sentences.en: And the next day, well-wishers are descending on the house.
sentences.zh: 第二天，满怀祝福的人们涌向这栋房子。

sentences.en: And Taddy said to one of them, do you think my father has gone?
sentences.zh: 塔迪对其中一个人说，你觉得我父亲去了吗？

sentences.en: I have not a doubt of it, the well-wisher said.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，那位祝福者说。

sentences.en: And Taddy said, then I'm glad he's gone there, for he never was happy after he came here to Washington.

sentences.en: And they pay him $12 to guide them to a plantation house owned by another Confederate bloke that they know.

sentences.en: And there this bloke who owns the plantation gets his overseer to take them to a pine thicket in the swamp.
sentences.zh: 然后，那个拥有种植园的家伙让他的工头把他们带到沼泽地里的松树丛中。

sentences.en: Has there been a film about this?
sentences.zh: 有没有关于这事的电影？

sentences.en: Surely.
sentences.zh: 当然有。

sentences.en: I think there's been a series, a Netflix series or something of that kind.
sentences.zh: 我想应该有一部剧，奈飞的剧或者类似的东西。

sentences.en: Oh, let's watch it.
sentences.zh: 哦，我们来看看吧。

sentences.en: I bet there should clearly be another one, a better one, because this is a great story.
sentences.zh: 我敢说肯定还得拍一部，一部更好的，因为这是一个绝佳的故事。

sentences.en: So they hide in this pine thicket.
sentences.zh: 所以他们躲在这片松树丛里。

sentences.en: And basically, their friends and Confederate agents are trying to figure out how to get them across the Potomac River into Virginia.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他们的朋友和邦联特工正想方设法带他们穿过波托马克河进入弗吉尼亚。

sentences.en: So they wait in this thicket for about four days and nights, I think.
sentences.zh: 所以我想他们在灌木丛里大约等了四天四夜。

sentences.en: And a local Confederate agent called Thomas Jones pitches up every now and again with food, and in particular with newspapers.
sentences.zh: 一个名叫托马斯·琼斯的当地邦联特工时不时会送来食物，特别是报纸。

sentences.en: So Booth has not been able to, you know, like any good actor, he's obsessed with his reviews.
sentences.zh: 所以布斯一直没法——你知道的，就像任何优秀的演员一样，他对自己的评价有着病态的执着。

sentences.en: He wants to read what people have written about him in the papers.
sentences.zh: 他想读读人们在报纸上对他的评价。

sentences.en: And he had written a letter to the newspapers explaining his reasons that he was the American Brutus.
sentences.zh: 他还给报社写了一封信，阐述自己的理由，称自己是美国的布鲁图斯。

sentences.en: And he's absolutely furious that they haven't printed it.
sentences.zh: 而他们居然没把信登出来，这让他气急败坏。

sentences.en: They haven't given him the airtime, as it were.
sentences.zh: 他们根本没给他所谓的出镜机会。

sentences.en: And it's at this point that he writes his first journal entry.
sentences.zh: 正是在这个时候，他写下了第一篇日记。

sentences.en: So this is not the one that you read.
sentences.zh: 所以这不是你读的那篇。

sentences.en: It's an earlier one.
sentences.zh: 这是一篇更早的。

sentences.en: And he explains, you know, why he did what he did.
sentences.zh: 他解释了，你知道的，他为什么要这么做。

sentences.en: He said,
sentences.zh: 他说，

sentences.en: Now, here's an interesting thing.
sentences.zh: 现在，这里有个有趣的事。

sentences.en: I shouted six Semper before I fired.
sentences.zh: 我开枪前大喊了六声“塞姆珀”。

sentences.en: Not afterwards.
sentences.zh: 而不是开枪后。

sentences.en: Every other account says he shouted six Semper to Iranis after he fired.
sentences.zh: 所有其他记录都说他是开枪后向伊拉尼斯大喊了六声“塞姆珀”。

sentences.en: So do you think his memory is playing tricks on him?
sentences.zh: 所以你觉得他的记忆出毛病了吗？

sentences.en: Possibly his memory is playing tricks on him.
sentences.zh: 他的记忆可能确实出毛病了。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: In jumping, I broke my leg.
sentences.zh: 跳跃时，我摔断了腿。

sentences.en: I passed all his pickets.
sentences.zh: 我通过了他所有的哨卡。

sentences.en: I rode 60 miles that night with the bone of my leg tearing the flesh at every jump.
sentences.zh: 那天晚上我骑了60英里，每一次跳跃都让断骨撕裂着肌肉。

sentences.en: I can never repent it.
sentences.zh: 我绝不后悔。

sentences.en: Our country owed all her trouble to him.
sentences.zh: 我们国家的所有麻烦都怪他。

sentences.en: And God simply made me the instrument of his punishment.
sentences.zh: 上帝只是让我成了惩罚他的工具。

sentences.en: There is a definite air of sort of hysteria, I think, about this entry.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这篇日记里有一种明显歇斯底里的气息。

sentences.en: You know, he's not thinking terribly clearly, I think it's fair to say.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我觉得可以公正地说，他当时的想法极其混乱。

sentences.en: Thursday the 20th.
sentences.zh: 20日，星期四。

sentences.en: Thomas Jones, the Confederate agent, his reports that Union troops are now scouring the woods in a nearby county.
sentences.zh: 邦联特工托马斯·琼斯报告说，联邦军队现在正在搜查附近县城的树林。

sentences.en: And he tells them they have to move.
sentences.zh: 他告诉他们必须转移。

sentences.en: They have to go across the river.
sentences.zh: 他们必须过河。

sentences.en: He's got a fishing boat down on the Potomac.
sentences.zh: 他在波托马克河上有一艘渔船。

sentences.en: And he pushes them off into the night on this fishing boat.
sentences.zh: 他在夜色中把他们推上这艘渔船，让他们出发。

sentences.en: It's very foggy.
sentences.zh: 雾非常大。

sentences.en: And the Potomac at this point is very wide.
sentences.zh: 而且这里的波托马克河非常宽。

sentences.en: And they get completely loSt.
sentences.zh: 结果他们彻底迷路了。

sentences.en: They row all night.
sentences.zh: 他们划了一夜的船。

sentences.en: And then they land.
sentences.zh: 然后他们上了岸。

sentences.en: And then when the day comes, they realize they're basically back where they started, but further away.
sentences.zh: 天亮时，他们发现自己基本上回到了出发点，只是离得更远了。

sentences.en: And they're still on the wrong side of the river.
sentences.zh: 而且他们仍然在河的错误一侧。

sentences.en: So the next night, Friday the 21st, Saturday the 22nd, they have another go.
sentences.zh: 所以在接下来的几个晚上，即21日星期五和22日星期六，他们又尝试了一次。

sentences.en: And they manage to row across this time.
sentences.zh: 这一次他们设法划了过去。

sentences.en: And they land.
sentences.zh: 然后他们上了岸。

sentences.en: Of course they land.
sentences.zh: 他们当然上岸了。

sentences.en: Somewhere called Gambo Creek in Virginia.
sentences.zh: 弗吉尼亚一个叫甘博溪的地方。

sentences.en: In the meantime, this is when Booth has written that second journal entry that you read so splendidly.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，布斯写下了你刚才声情并茂朗读的第二篇日记。

sentences.en: So the tone here, I think, you did it in a very ebullient style.
sentences.zh: 所以这里的基调，我觉得，你读得非常热情洋溢。

sentences.en: Brighton Blessed style.
sentences.zh: 布赖顿·布莱斯式的风格。

sentences.en: I think it's fair to say.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这么说很公平。

sentences.en: But actually, I think he's very bedraggled and miserable at this point.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，我觉得他这时候蓬头垢面、痛苦不堪。

sentences.en: Oh.
sentences.zh: 哦。

sentences.en: All this stuff about being hunted by a dog and all this.
sentences.zh: 所有关于被狗追之类的破事。

sentences.en: So I didn't think through what his motivation was.
sentences.zh: 所以我没有仔细琢磨他的动机是什么。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: It wasn't method acting.
sentences.zh: 这不是方法派表演。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Daniel Day-Lewis wouldn't approve of that at all.
sentences.zh: 丹尼尔·戴-刘易斯绝对不会赞同这种做法。

sentences.en: No, he wouldn't.
sentences.zh: 没错，他才不会。

sentences.en: I should have prepared for it by spending a week being hunted by dogs through brushwood.
sentences.zh: 我本来应该花一个星期在灌木丛里被狗追，以此来做好准备。

sentences.en: And then I could have done it justice.
sentences.zh: 然后我才能演好它。

sentences.en: Oh, I've let you down, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 哦，我让你失望了，多米尼克。

sentences.en: I'm really sorry.
sentences.zh: 真的很抱歉。

sentences.en: You should have recorded the previous episode, which we'd just done, in character.
sentences.zh: 你本该在上一集里就保持这种角色状态的，我们刚刚才录完。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: As John Wilkes Booth to prepare you.
sentences.zh: 以约翰·威尔克斯·布斯的身份来为你做准备。

sentences.en: I should have done.
sentences.zh: 我本该这么做的。

sentences.en: Damn.
sentences.zh: 该死。

sentences.en: So anyway, he feels very sorry for himself.
sentences.zh: 总之，他非常顾影自怜。

sentences.en: I'm abandoned with the curse of Cain upon me.
sentences.zh: 我被抛弃了，背负着该隐的诅咒。

sentences.en: When if the world knew my heart, that one blow would have made me great.
sentences.zh: 如果世人了解我的内心，那一击本该让我名垂青史。

sentences.en: Though I did desire no greatness.
sentences.zh: 虽然我并渴望什么伟大。

sentences.en: And then he says, I have too great a soul to die like a criminal.
sentences.zh: 然后他说，我有太高尚的灵魂，不能像个罪犯一样死去。

sentences.en: He thinks a lot of himself, I think it's fair to say.
sentences.zh: 我觉得可以说，他自我感觉极其良好。

sentences.en: He does.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So for two days, they continue south.
sentences.zh: 于是他们继续向南逃了两天。

sentences.en: And on the Sunday night, the 23rd, he lets himself down, behaves very poorly.
sentences.zh: 在23日星期日晚上，他自甘堕落，表现得非常糟糕。

sentences.en: What do you mean he lets himself down?
sentences.zh: 你什么意思，他自甘堕落？

sentences.en: He's just shot Abraham Lincoln.
sentences.zh: 他刚枪杀亚伯拉罕·林肯。

sentences.en: That's true.
sentences.zh: 也对。

sentences.en: Of course he's let himself down.
sentences.zh: 他当然是自甘堕落了。

sentences.en: I think worse of him for this, actually.
sentences.zh: 实际上，我对他的看法更差了。

sentences.en: I think worse of him for this.
sentences.zh: 我对他的看法更差了。

sentences.en: You see, he arrives at the cabin of a free black family called the Lucases.
sentences.zh: 你看，他来到了一户名叫卢卡斯的自由黑人家庭的小木屋前。

sentences.en: And he and Harold threaten the father, William Lucas, at knife point and drive the whole family into the woods so they can sleep in their cabin.
sentences.zh: 他和杰拉尔德用刀威胁父亲威廉·卢卡斯，把全家人赶进树林，好让他们自己睡在木屋里。

sentences.en: That is poor.
sentences.zh: 这太卑鄙了。

sentences.en: It is poor.
sentences.zh: 确实卑鄙。

sentences.en: But I mean, at least he doesn't kill William Lucas.
sentences.zh: 不过我是说，至少他没杀了威廉·卢卡斯。

sentences.en: I agree.
sentences.zh: 我同意。

sentences.en: He's not coming across well from this series.
sentences.zh: 从这部剧来看，他的形象不太光彩。

sentences.en: It reflects really badly on him.
sentences.zh: 这把他的形象衬托得极其糟糕。

sentences.en: It reflects really badly.
sentences.zh: 衬托得太糟糕了。

sentences.en: Yeah, I accept that.
sentences.zh: 对，我承认这一点。

sentences.en: The next day, Monday the 24th, he and Harold meet three Confederate soldiers who lead them to a tobacco farm, inevitably called Locust Hill.
sentences.zh: 第二天，即24日星期一，他和杰拉尔德遇到了三名邦联士兵，他们把两人带到了一座名为“蝗虫山”的烟草农场，这名字真是太应景了。

sentences.en: This is the world's most American story.
sentences.zh: 这就是全世界最美国的故事。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实是。

sentences.en: Locust Hill.
sentences.zh: 蝗虫山。

sentences.en: And it's owned by a man who actually has a reasonable name, Richard Garrett.
sentences.zh: 农场主的名字其实挺正常的，叫理查德·加勒特。

sentences.en: That's disappointing.
sentences.zh: 这挺让人失望的。

sentences.en: Booth says, I'm a wounded Confederate soldier.
sentences.zh: 布斯说：“我是个受伤的邦联士兵。”

sentences.en: And Garrett says, fine, you can stay.
sentences.zh: 加勒特说：“行吧，你可以留下来。”

sentences.en: Harold actually goes off with his other Confederate soldiers into the nearby town, which is called Bowling Green.
sentences.zh: 杰拉尔德实际上和另外几名邦联士兵去了附近的一个小镇，名叫鲍灵格林。

sentences.en: So Garrett doesn't say, if you're a Confederate soldier, why are you wearing evening dress?
sentences.zh: 所以加勒特没有问，如果你是个邦联士兵，为什么穿得像去参加晚宴？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对啊。

sentences.en: Why are you dressed like the Phantom of the Opera?
sentences.zh: 为什么你打扮得像歌剧魅影？

sentences.en: No, he doesn't.
sentences.zh: 不，他没问。

sentences.en: Actually, and at first it's lovely, sweetness and light.
sentences.zh: 其实一开始挺美好的，一团和气。

sentences.en: So Booth has a nice reSt.
sentences.zh: 所以布斯好好休息了一下。

sentences.en: He has a nice breakfaSt.
sentences.zh: 他吃了一顿丰盛的早餐。

sentences.en: And then he plays with Garrett's children on the lawn.
sentences.zh: 然后他在草坪上和加勒特的孩子们一起玩。

sentences.en: So maybe his leg is a bit better.
sentences.zh: 所以也许他的腿稍微好一点了。

sentences.en: But then things start to unravel.
sentences.zh: 但随后事情开始急转直下。

sentences.en: Harold and the soldiers come back to the Garrett farm, to Locust Hill.
sentences.zh: 杰拉尔德和士兵们回到了加勒特农场，也就是蝗虫山。

sentences.en: And they say, there's Union cavalry in the area.
sentences.zh: 他们说，附近有联邦骑兵。

sentences.en: And Booth panics and he rushes off to hide in the woods.
sentences.zh: 布斯吓得惊慌失措，急忙逃进树林里躲藏起来。

sentences.en: And at this point, the Garrett family become very suspicious.
sentences.zh: 就在这时，加勒特一家开始起疑心了。

sentences.en: If he's just an ordinary Confederate soldier, you know, why would he have panicked and run away to the woods?
sentences.zh: 如果他只是个普通的邦联士兵，你知道的，他为什么会惊慌失措地逃进树林呢？

sentences.en: The war's kind of over.
sentences.zh: 战争差不多已经结束了。

sentences.en: You know, it's very low risk, strange behavior.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，风险很低，这行为太奇怪了。

sentences.en: When he finally emerges, they say, are you really in the Confederate army?
sentences.zh: 当他终于现身时，他们问：“你真的是邦联军队的吗？”

sentences.en: He says, oh yeah.
sentences.zh: 他说：“哦，当然是。”

sentences.en: I was in, this is where his acting skills come in.
sentences.zh: 我曾经在——这就是他展现演技的时候了。

sentences.en: He says, I was in Captain Robinson's company of the 30th Virginia.
sentences.zh: 他说：“我曾在弗吉尼亚第30团罗宾逊上尉的连队服役。”

sentences.en: But as luck would have it, Richard Garrett's son, Jack, is a Confederate soldier.
sentences.zh: 但很不巧的是，理查德·加勒特的儿子杰克正是一名邦联士兵。

sentences.en: And he knows that unit.
sentences.zh: 他知道那个部队。

sentences.en: And he knows there is no such captain.
sentences.zh: 而且他知道根本没有这么个上尉。

sentences.en: So they have a massive argument.
sentences.zh: 于是他们爆发了一场大争吵。

sentences.en: And the Garretts eventually say, right, okay, you guys can stay one more night.
sentences.zh: 加勒特一家最终说道：“好吧，你们可以在这再呆一晚。”

sentences.en: We're not going to have you in the house.
sentences.zh: “我们绝不让你们进屋。”

sentences.en: You can stay in the tobacco barn.
sentences.zh: “你们可以睡在烟草仓库里。”

sentences.en: But the Garretts now think that these blokes are probably horse thieves.
sentences.zh: 但加勒特现在觉得这两个家伙很可能是偷马贼。

sentences.en: So they lock the barn door once Booth and Herald are inside.
sentences.zh: 所以在布斯和杰拉尔德进去后，他们把仓库门给锁上了。

sentences.en: Now, meanwhile, in the nearby town.
sentences.zh: 现在，与此同时，在附近的小镇上。

sentences.en: What's the nearby town called, Dominic?
sentences.zh: 附近那个小镇叫什么来着，多米尼克？

sentences.en: Bowling Green.
sentences.zh: 鲍灵格林。

sentences.en: It's unbelievable.
sentences.zh: 这简直难以置信。

sentences.en: Officers of the National Detective Police and a detachment of the 16th New York Cavalry have arrived to hunt for the fugitives.
sentences.zh: 国家侦探警察局的官员和纽约第16骑兵队的分队已经抵达，开始搜捕逃犯。

sentences.en: And they talk to these three Confederate soldiers who had helped Booth and Herald and basically get the truth out of them.
sentences.zh: 他们与曾经帮助过布斯和杰拉尔德的那三名邦联士兵交谈，基本上逼问出了真相。

sentences.en: It takes them two hours to ride to Locust Hill Farm.
sentences.zh: 他们骑马花了两个小时才赶到蝗虫山农场。

sentences.en: And they arrive at about two in the morning.
sentences.zh: 他们在凌晨两点左右抵达。

sentences.en: They surround the house.
sentences.zh: 他们包围了房子。

sentences.en: They drag the Garretts out of bed.
sentences.zh: 他们把加勒特一家从床上拖了起来。

sentences.en: And they basically say to Richard Garrett, if you don't tell us where these guys are, we will hang you right here.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上对理查德·加勒特说，如果你不告诉我们这些家伙在哪，我们现在就把你吊死在这里。

sentences.en: Jack Garrett, this Confederate soldier, who's still wearing his Confederate uniform, comes out.
sentences.zh: 杰克·加勒特，这个穿着邦联军服的邦联士兵走了出来。

sentences.en: And he says, Father, just tell them.
sentences.zh: 他说，神父，直接告诉他们吧。

sentences.en: So they go to the barn.
sentences.zh: 于是他们去了谷仓。

sentences.en: And the detectives send Jack Garrett to speak to the fugitives, say, come out.
sentences.zh: 侦探们派杰克·加勒特去跟逃亡者谈话，让他们出来。

sentences.en: They won't come out.
sentences.zh: 他们就是不肯出来。

sentences.en: Then the chief of the detectives, who's called Luther Byron Baker, he shouts into the barn.
sentences.zh: 接着，被称为卢瑟·拜伦·贝克的侦探长朝着谷仓大喊。

sentences.en: He says, Surrender, come out.
sentences.zh: 他说，投降吧，出来。

sentences.en: And if you don't come out, I'll burn this barn down.
sentences.zh: 如果你们不出来，我就把这个谷仓烧了。

sentences.en: You've got 15 minutes.
sentences.zh: 你们还有15分钟。

sentences.en: Herald wants to give up.
sentences.zh: 赫罗尔德想要放弃。

sentences.en: Booth says, No, no, don't give up.
sentences.zh: 布思说，不，不，不要放弃。

sentences.en: Don't give up, whispering to him.
sentences.zh: 别放弃，他低声对他说。

sentences.en: Luther Byron Baker says, I'm going to start burning this barn down.
sentences.zh: 卢瑟·拜伦·贝克说，我要开始烧这个谷仓了。

sentences.en: And Booth shouts back.
sentences.zh: 布思大声回喊。

sentences.en: He says, Captain, that's rather rough.
sentences.zh: 他说，队长，这也太粗暴了吧。

sentences.en: I'm nothing but a cripple.
sentences.zh: 我不过是个残废。

sentences.en: I have but one leg.
sentences.zh: 我只有一条腿。

sentences.en: You ought to give me a chance for a fair fight.
sentences.zh: 你们应该给我一个公平决斗的机会。

sentences.en: And Baker says, Listen, you've got five minutes, and I'm going to burn this bloody barn down.
sentences.zh: 贝克说，听着，你们还有五分钟，我就要把这该死的谷仓烧了。

sentences.en: Booth is playing for time, making all sorts of complaints and stuff.
sentences.zh: 布思在拖延时间，各种抱怨个没完。

sentences.en: And eventually, they pile brushwood against the barn, and one of them sets it alight.
sentences.zh: 最终，他们在谷仓旁堆起干柴，其中一人点燃了它。

sentences.en: At this point, Herald panics.
sentences.zh: 此时，赫罗尔德慌了神。

sentences.en: He runs to the door.
sentences.zh: 他跑到门边。

sentences.en: Let me out, let me out.
sentences.zh: 放我出去，放我出去。

sentences.en: He manages to get out, and the troopers grab him and tie him up.
sentences.zh: 他设法逃了出去，骑兵们一把抓住他并把他捆了起来。

sentences.en: So now there's just Booth.
sentences.zh: 所以现在只剩下布思了。

sentences.en: And Booth, remember, has a rifle.
sentences.zh: 别忘了，布思手里有一支步枪。

sentences.en: He has one of his rifles from the tavern.
sentences.zh: 他带着从酒馆拿来的一支步枪。

sentences.en: The fire is spreading now across the barn.
sentences.zh: 大火现在正蔓延过整个谷仓。

sentences.en: It spreads to the rafters.
sentences.zh: 火势蔓延到了屋顶的椽子上。

sentences.en: The barn is lit up with this weird glow.
sentences.zh: 谷仓被这种奇异的火光照亮了。

sentences.en: And through the cracks in the timbers, the soldiers can see Booth.
sentences.zh: 透过木板的缝隙，士兵们可以看到布思。

sentences.en: As Michael Kaufman says in his book, he's trapped like a wild animal, kind of darting around, looking for a place to escape.
sentences.zh: 正如迈克尔·考夫曼在他的书中所说，他像一只野兽一样被困住，到处乱窜，寻找逃跑的地方。

sentences.en: And, Dominic, it is at this point that the moment long-term fans of the rest of history have been looking forward to.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，正是在这个时候，历史长剧的忠实粉丝们翘首以盼的时刻到了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Because it is now that one of history's top ten eunuchs makes his appearance in this series.
sentences.zh: 因为正是现在，历史上的十大阉人之一在这部剧里登场了。

sentences.en: Yes, Sergeant Boston Corbett.
sentences.zh: 没错，波士顿·科比特中士。

sentences.en: Which you would say is a classic American name, but actually is English.
sentences.zh: 你可能会说这是一个经典的美国名字，但实际上它是英国的。

sentences.en: He's a Londoner.
sentences.zh: 他是伦敦人。

sentences.en: The distinctive thing about Boston Corbett, so he's a trooper there with the cavalry, is that he is literally as mad as a hatter.
sentences.zh: 关于波士顿·科比特，他当时是骑兵团的一名骑兵，他最独特的地方在于他简直疯得像个帽匠。

sentences.en: Because he is a hatter, right?
sentences.zh: 因为他本来就是个帽匠，对吧？

sentences.en: He had worked as a milliner in New York, and he'd been driven mad by the mercury.
sentences.zh: 他曾在纽约当过女帽商，而且他已经被水银毒疯了。

sentences.en: I think they used mercury for fur, didn't they?
sentences.zh: 我想他们在处理皮毛时用过水银，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: To cure the fur in hats.
sentences.zh: 用来处理帽子上的皮毛。

sentences.en: We did an episode on that.
sentences.zh: 我们专门做过一期节目。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And he became a religious maniac.
sentences.zh: 然后他变成了一个宗教狂热分子。

sentences.en: That is to say, a MethodiSt.
sentences.zh: 也就是卫理公会信徒。

sentences.en: Apologies to any Methodist listeners for Dominic's abuse.
sentences.zh: 向任何因多米尼克的言论而受到冒犯的卫理公会听众道歉。

sentences.en: While pursuing his Methodism in Boston, Massachusetts, he castrated himself with a pair of scissors, didn't he?
sentences.zh: 当他在马萨诸塞州波士顿继续他的卫理公会信仰时，他用一把剪刀阉割了自己，对吧？

sentences.en: He did.
sentences.zh: 他确实这么做了。

sentences.en: And so, I mean, it's a whole scissors theme, actually, in our show.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，我们节目里其实有个贯穿始终的“剪刀”主题。

sentences.en: Because remember, Charles XII of Sweden cut his own foot open with some scissors.
sentences.zh: 因为记住，瑞典的查理十二世曾用一把剪刀划破了自己的脚。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But this is much more extreme.
sentences.zh: 但这个要极端得多。

sentences.en: He unmanned himself with these scissors.
sentences.zh: 他用这把剪刀切掉了自己的命根子。

sentences.en: Then he enlisted in the Union Army, became a prisoner of war at Andersonville Prison, a great sort of notorious Confederate prison camp.
sentences.zh: 后来他加入了联邦军队，在安德森维尔战俘营——一个臭名昭著的邦联战俘营——成了战俘。

sentences.en: And then he was exchanged just in time to serve in the detachment sent to capture Booth.
sentences.zh: 然后他恰好被交换回来，得以在抓捕布思的分队里服役。

sentences.en: So, Boston Corbett is looking through the cracks in the timbers, and he sees Booth raise his rifle and move towards the door.
sentences.zh: 因此，波士顿·科比特透过木板的缝隙望进去，看到布思举起步枪向门口走去。

sentences.en: Now, almost certainly, Booth was surrendering, was planning to surrender, I think.
sentences.zh: 现在，几乎可以肯定的是，布思当时是在投降，正计划投降，我认为是这样。

sentences.en: Their barn is on fire.
sentences.zh: 他们的谷仓着火了。

sentences.en: Boston Corbett just fired.
sentences.zh: 波士顿·科比特直接开枪了。

sentences.en: He fired through the gaps in the timbers, his revolver, and Booth is down.
sentences.zh: 他用左轮手枪透过木板的缝隙开枪，布思倒下了。

sentences.en: And Dominic, there's never been any kind of notion that he's a kind of Jack Ruby figure employed to silence him.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，从来没有任何人认为他是那种被雇来灭口的杰克·鲁比式的人物。

sentences.en: Working for Mrs. Ulysses S.
sentences.zh: 为尤利西斯·S·格兰特

sentences.en: Grant.
sentences.zh: 夫人的手下工作。

sentences.en: That's not part of conspiracy theory law.
sentences.zh: 这不属于阴谋论的范畴。

sentences.en: I think only by you, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我想大概只有你这么认为，汤姆。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, write in if there is a conspiracy theory along that line.
sentences.zh: 我是说，如果真有这方面的阴谋论，大家可以写信来。

sentences.en: This is American history.
sentences.zh: 这是美国历史。

sentences.en: Therefore, there are almost certainly some mad theories out there, I would imagine.
sentences.zh: 因此，我猜外面几乎肯定流传着一些疯狂的理论。

sentences.en: Anyway, maybe that bloke they carry out is not John Wilkes Booth.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，也许他们抬出来的那个家伙根本不是约翰·威尔克斯·布思。

sentences.en: Maybe the real John Wilkes Booth is somewhere else.
sentences.zh: 也许真正的约翰·威尔克斯·布思在别的什么地方。

sentences.en: Who knows?
sentences.zh: 谁知道呢？

sentences.en: Anyway, they carry him out.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，他们把他抬了出来。

sentences.en: Boston Corbett has shot him in the neck.
sentences.zh: 波士顿·科比特击中了的他的脖子。

sentences.en: The bullet went through his neck and through his spinal column.
sentences.zh: 子弹穿过了他的脖子和脊椎。

sentences.en: So he's dying.
sentences.zh: 所以他快要死了。

sentences.en: One of the detectives who has the excellent name, Everton Conga.
sentences.zh: 其中一位侦探名字很好听，叫埃弗顿·孔加。

sentences.en: Everton Conga.
sentences.zh: 埃弗顿·孔加。

sentences.en: Oh, what is it with these names?
sentences.zh: 噢，这些名字是怎么回事？

sentences.en: There's a eunuch in there.
sentences.zh: 里面有个阉人。

sentences.en: There's someone with the name of Conga.
sentences.zh: 还有个叫孔加的人。

sentences.en: Boston Corbett and Everton Conga.
sentences.zh: 波士顿·科比特和埃弗顿·孔加。

sentences.en: There's far too many surnames in those names.
sentences.zh: 这些名字里的姓氏也太多了吧。

sentences.en: That's four people.
sentences.zh: 那可是四个人。

sentences.en: They could be a crime-fighting duo.
sentences.zh: 他们可以组成一个打击犯罪的二人组。

sentences.en: The eunuch and the Conga.
sentences.zh: 太监与孔加。

sentences.en: Solving crime in Reconstruction America.
sentences.zh: 在重建时期的美国打击犯罪。

sentences.en: Okay, Everton Conga kneels over him and Booth whispers,
sentences.zh: 好了，埃弗顿·孔加俯身跪在他身上，布思低声说道，

sentences.en: Tell my mother that I did it for my country.
sentences.zh: 告诉我的母亲，我是为了国家才这么做的。

sentences.en: Tell my mother that I'd die for my country.
sentences.zh: 告诉我的母亲，我愿为国牺牲。

sentences.en: So he's a mummy's boy right to the end.
sentences.zh: 所以他直到最后还是个恋母的小男孩。

sentences.en: And it took hours for him to die.
sentences.zh: 他花了几个小时才死去。

sentences.en: He kept repeating that line about his mother and his country.
sentences.zh: 他一直在重复那句关于他的母亲和国家的话。

sentences.en: But then as dawn breaks, again, perfect for Hollywood cinematographer.
sentences.zh: 但随着黎明破晓，再次完美契合好莱坞摄影师的审美。

sentences.en: As dawn breaks, he whispers,
sentences.zh: 随着黎明破晓，他低声呢喃，

sentences.en: Useless, useless.
sentences.zh: 没用，没用。

sentences.en: And then he dies.
sentences.zh: 然后他就死了。

sentences.en: That's the end of John Wilkes Booth.
sentences.zh: 这就是约翰·威尔克斯·布思的结局。

sentences.en: Now, the thing is, his story is so rich, actually.
sentences.zh: 问题是，他的故事其实非常丰富。

sentences.en: This book that I mentioned by Michael Kaufman, American Brutus, is brilliant.
sentences.zh: 我提到的这本迈克尔·考夫曼写的书《美国布鲁图斯》太棒了。

sentences.en: He thinks the key to Booth is that he was an actor.
sentences.zh: 他认为理解布思的关键在于他是个演员。

sentences.en: That basically, he lived in a world of make-believe.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他生活在一个幻想的世界里。

sentences.en: That his identity as a Southern gentleman was a complete fiction.
sentences.zh: 他作为南方绅士的身份完全是个虚构。

sentences.en: He'd never lived in the South properly.
sentences.zh: 他从来没有真正在南方生活过。

sentences.en: He came from a border state.
sentences.zh: 他来自一个边境州。

sentences.en: He'd never had a great success in the South.
sentences.zh: 他从未在南方取得过什么巨大的成功。

sentences.en: All his success was in the North.
sentences.zh: 他所有的成功都在北方。

sentences.en: So he's basically a Yankee.
sentences.zh: 所以他基本上是个北方佬。

sentences.en: Yeah, but he's invented this fantasy life for himself.
sentences.zh: 对，但他为自己编造了这样一段魔幻的生活。

sentences.en: And as Kaufman says, he constructed a dramatic persona for himself rather than accept the truth that he was a hot-headed loser who only talked while others gave their lives.
sentences.zh: 正如考夫曼所说，他为自己构建了一个戏剧化的人设，却不愿接受这样一个事实：他不过是个头脑发热的失败者，只会动嘴皮子，而别人却在付出生命。

sentences.en: His title is American Brutus.
sentences.zh: 他的书名是《美国布鲁图斯》。

sentences.en: And of course, the great irony is that John Wilkes Booth dreamt of being Brutus, but it never occurred to him that Brutus was a failure.
sentences.zh: 当然，最大的讽刺在于，约翰·威尔克斯·布思梦想成为布鲁图斯，却从未想过布鲁图斯其实是个失败者。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That Brutus turned Caesar into a martyr.
sentences.zh: 布鲁图斯把凯撒变成了一个殉道者。

sentences.en: And that actually, his actions hastened the end of the Roman Republic.
sentences.zh: 而实际上，他的行动加速了罗马共和国的灭亡。

sentences.en: That he destroyed his own cause.
sentences.zh: 他毁了自己的事业。

sentences.en: And of course, that's what John Wilkes Booth does to some degree.
sentences.zh: 当然，约翰·威尔克斯·布思在某种程度上也是这么做的。

sentences.en: Now, the real question that hangs over all this is, which is a shame to be asking this question after we've spent a lot of time on this show.
sentences.zh: 现在，悬在这一切之上的真正问题是——在这个节目上花了很多时间之后再问这个问题未免有些遗憾——

sentences.en: Did it matter?
sentences.zh: 这重要吗？

sentences.en: Is it of any importance?
sentences.zh: 这有什么重要意义吗？

sentences.en: And of course, a lot of American listeners will say that it mattered enormously.
sentences.zh: 当然，许多美国听众会说这极其重要。

sentences.en: Because as with John F.
sentences.zh: 因为就像约翰·F·

sentences.en: Kennedy, you know, with John F.
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪一样，你知道的，对于约翰·F·

sentences.en: Kennedy, there is this sort of fantasy.
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪，一直存在着这样一种幻想。

sentences.en: If Kennedy lives, you don't get Vietnam.
sentences.zh: 如果肯尼迪活着，就不会有越南战争。

sentences.en: You don't get the Vietnam War.
sentences.zh: 就不会卷入越战。

sentences.en: And the sort of darker turn of the late 60s and Nixon and everything that follows.
sentences.zh: 也不会有60年代后期那种更黑暗的转折、尼克尔逊以及随之而来的一切。

sentences.en: And the fantasy that's so common in Lincoln's death is, Lincoln lives and the South is beaten.
sentences.zh: 关于林肯之死，最常见的幻想就是：林肯活着，南方被打败。

sentences.en: But Lincoln controls Reconstruction.
sentences.zh: 但林肯掌控了重建工作。

sentences.en: Black Americans are given the vote.
sentences.zh: 黑人美国人获得了投票权。

sentences.en: The Confederates never regained control of the Southern states.
sentences.zh: 邦联分子再也没有重新夺回南方各州的控制权。

sentences.en: There is no segregation.
sentences.zh: 没有种族隔离。

sentences.en: The Jim Crow laws of the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 没有20世纪的吉姆·克劳法。

sentences.en: That actually all is sweetness and light.
sentences.zh: 一切实际上都甜美而光明。

sentences.en: And personally, I find this unbelievably unconvincing and implausible.
sentences.zh: 就我个人而言，我觉得这简直难以置信、荒谬不经。

sentences.en: I think, first of all, because like the Kennedy sort of fantasies, it massively exaggerates the power of the presidency.
sentences.zh: 首先我认为，就像关于肯尼迪的种种幻想一样，这极大地夸大了总统的权力。

sentences.en: What actually happens is Reconstruction ends up being a huge power struggle between the White House and Congress, which Congress actually wins.
sentences.zh: 实际发生的情况是，重建最终成了白宫与国会之间的一场巨大权力斗争，而国会实际上赢了。

sentences.en: And Lincoln's successor, Andrew Johnson, ends up being impeached.
sentences.zh: 林肯的继任者安德鲁·约翰逊最终遭到弹劾。

sentences.en: So there's a real irony there that Lincoln is murdered for being a tyrant, for being a Caesar.
sentences.zh: 所以这里有一个巨大的讽刺：林肯被谋杀是因为他被视为暴君，被视为凯撒。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But there's actually the problem that he would have faced is that he's not nearly autocratic enough.
sentences.zh: 但实际上他将面临的问题是，他根本不够独裁。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that actually, as soon as the war was over, Congress would have sought to roll back a lot of his, what they saw as his more imperial powers.
sentences.zh: 实际上，战争一结束，国会就会试图剥夺他的许多权力——那些国会认为是他更加帝王般的权力。

sentences.en: The second thing, I think the sort of fantasy tributes Lincoln with superhuman political skills that no human being ever possessed.
sentences.zh: 第二点，我认为这种幻想赋予了林肯任何人类都不曾拥有的超人政治技能。

sentences.en: Because Lincoln is a lame duck president.
sentences.zh: 因为林肯是一位跛脚鸭总统。

sentences.en: And he's already facing massive opposition in Congress.
sentences.zh: 而且他当时在国会就已经面临着巨大的反对声浪。

sentences.en: Now, a lot of people expect that from the Democrats who think he's a dictator.
sentences.zh: 现在，很多人对民主党人有这种期望，他们认为他是个独裁者。

sentences.en: But the really interesting thing that I think would surprise a lot of listeners is the opposition from radicals in his own party.
sentences.zh: 但真正有趣、而且我认为会让很多听众感到惊讶的是，他党内的激进派对他的反对。

sentences.en: So this is an extraordinary thing, that when he dies, a lot of the keenest abolitionists in the Republican Party are actually delighted.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一件很了不起的事，当他死后，共和党内许多最热心的废奴主义者其实感到非常高兴。

sentences.en: They held a meeting after his death, and the Indiana Congressman George Julian recorded, quote, the universal feeling that his death is a godsend.
sentences.zh: 他在死后举行了一次会议，印第安纳州众议员乔治·朱利安记录道，引用原话，“普遍的感觉是他的死真是天赐良机”。

sentences.en: Because many of them think, quite wrongly, that his vice president will do a better job.
sentences.zh: 因为他们中的许多人错误地认为，他的副总统会做得更好。

sentences.en: But I mean, imagine if you'd had, I don't know, members of the FBI or the CIA meeting up and saying that Kennedy's death was a godsend.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，想象一下，如果当时有，我不知道，联邦调查局或中央情报局的成员聚在一起说肯尼迪的死是个天赐良机。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: You would suspect a conspiracy.
sentences.zh: 你会怀疑这是一场阴谋。

sentences.en: You think the radical Republicans killed Abraham Lincoln?
sentences.zh: 你觉得是激进的共和党人杀了亚伯拉罕·林肯？

sentences.en: The whole thing is just spiraling out of control here.
sentences.zh: 整件事在这里简直失控了。

sentences.en: I mean, actually, if you want evidence, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，实际上，如果你想要证据的话，汤姆。

sentences.en: So, Zachariah Chandler, senator from Michigan.
sentences.zh: 所以，扎卡里亚·钱德勒，来自密歇根州的参议员。

sentences.en: God continued Mr. Lincoln in office as long as he was useful, and then substituted a better man to finish the work.
sentences.zh: “上帝让林肯先生继续在任，只要他还有用，然后换上了一个更好的人来完成这项工作。”

sentences.en: Benjamin Wade, senator from Ohio.
sentences.zh: 本杰明·韦德，来自俄亥俄州的参议员。

sentences.en: By the gods, there will be no trouble now in running the government.
sentences.zh: “凭老天爷发誓，现在治理政府不会再有任何麻烦了。”

sentences.en: Mr. Lincoln had too much of human kindness in him to deal with his infamous traitors.
sentences.zh: “林肯先生身上有着太多的人类同情心，无法对付那些可恶的叛徒。”

sentences.en: In other words, the radical Republicans are much less on Lincoln's team than we often think.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，激进的共和党人远没有我们想象的那么支持林肯。

sentences.en: And they would probably have fallen out with him in the next few months or years over Reconstruction.
sentences.zh: 而且在接下来的几个月或几年里，他们很可能会因为重建问题而与他翻脸。

sentences.en: But the biggest thing, actually, the issue of the South and racism, white supremacy, it can't be fixed by one man.
sentences.zh: 但最重要的事情，实际上，南方问题、种族主义和白人至上，不是一个人能解决的。

sentences.en: Because it would have taken, I think, a long-term military regime in the southern states committed to black equality to change things.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为，这需要在南方各州长期维持一个致力于黑人平等的军事政权，才能改变现状。

sentences.en: And the North was never, ever going to accept such a political and financial commitment.
sentences.zh: 而北方永远、永远不会接受这样的政治和财政承诺。

sentences.en: The white South would always have resisted.
sentences.zh: 南方白人永远都会反抗。

sentences.en: There would always have been paramilitary groups like the Ku Klux Klan.
sentences.zh: 永远都会有像三K党这样的准军事组织。

sentences.en: And we actually know from Lincoln's public statements, that's the reason I mentioned them in the first episode,
sentences.zh: 其实我们从林肯的公开声明中就知道，这也是我在第一集里提到他们的原因，

sentences.en: he's desperate to get the white South integrated as quickly as possible to return to what he sees as harmony and reconciliation.
sentences.zh: 他极其渴望尽快让南方白人融入进来，回到他视为和谐与和解的状态。

sentences.en: So the destiny of the United States as a continental power, even to Lincoln, is more significant than establishing racial equality?
sentences.zh: 所以，美国作为大陆强国的命运，对林肯来说，甚至比确立种族平等更重要？

sentences.en: Yes, I would say so, actually.
sentences.zh: 是的，我可以说确实如此。

sentences.en: Now, I don't say that to diminish him.
sentences.zh: 我这么说并不是为了贬低他。

sentences.en: He's a practical politician.
sentences.zh: 他是个务实的政治家。

sentences.en: He's choosing from different priorities.
sentences.zh: 他在不同的优先事项中做出选择。

sentences.en: I think he is committed to racial equality, but gradually.
sentences.zh: 我认为他致力于种族平等，但这是渐进的。

sentences.en: And I think he would have found the challenge just as complex and demanding as his successors did, as Ulysses S.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为他会发现这个挑战和他的继任者们一样复杂和苛刻，就像尤利西斯·S·

sentences.en: Grant did, actually, when he became president.
sentences.zh: 格兰特当上总统后所经历的那样。

sentences.en: So in a way, you can argue that, as with Kennedy, his killer actually does him a real favor.
sentences.zh: 所以在某种程度上，你可以说，就像肯尼迪一样，他的凶手实际上帮了他一个大忙。

sentences.en: You know, John Wilkes Booth turns him into a martyr because there's nothing the world likes more than a kind of slain hero, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道，约翰·威尔克斯·布思把他变成了一个烈士，因为世界上没有比一个遇害的英雄更让人喜闻乐见的东西了，对吧？

sentences.en: As you implied in the first episode, there's nothing you enjoy more than an idol with feet of clay.
sentences.zh: 正如你在第一集所暗示的，没有什么比一个有脚泥的偶像更让人津津乐道的了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But what we've just been talking about in the relation to Lincoln, do you think that diminishes him?
sentences.zh: 但我们刚刚讨论的关于林肯的事，你觉得这会贬低他吗？

sentences.en: Does that diminish his reputation or not?
sentences.zh: 这会损害他的声誉吗？

sentences.en: Do you think Lincoln deserves the reputation that he has, not just in America, but really across the world?
sentences.zh: 你认为林肯配得上他在美国乃至全世界享有的声誉吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think he does, actually.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为他当之无愧。

sentences.en: Michael Burlingame, in this book that I've mentioned a few times, brilliant biography, he says Lincoln had a personality that you very rarely find in politics,
sentences.zh: 迈克尔·伯林盖姆在我提到过几次的那本精彩传记里说，林肯拥有在政坛极其罕见的个性，

sentences.en: as somebody who is firmly committed to a vision, who has the practical, pragmatic skills in order to achieve it, but is a fully kind of realized human being,
sentences.zh: 作为一个人，他坚定地致力于某个愿景，拥有实现这一愿景的实用、务实的技巧，但同时又是一个完全成熟的人，

sentences.en: being reflective, humble, thoughtful, with a kind of wry sense of his own place in the grand scheme of things.
sentences.zh: 会反思、谦逊、深思熟虑，对自己在宏伟计划中的位置有一种苦涩而清醒的幽默感。

sentences.en: You know, not without ego, of course, none of us are, but he's able to hold his ego in check.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当然也不是没有自我，我们谁都有，但他能控制住自己的自我。

sentences.en: A really impressive person, I would say.
sentences.zh: 一个非常令人印象深刻的人，我想这么说。

sentences.en: I don't know huge amounts about his life, but everything that I read about him, two things strike me.
sentences.zh: 我对他的生平了解不多，但我读到的关于他的所有内容中，有两点让我印象深刻。

sentences.en: One is that he has this incredible ability that all the really great, morally profound American politicians have had.
sentences.zh: 一个是他拥有所有真正伟大、具有道德深度的美国政治家所具备的那种不可思议的能力。

sentences.en: So we did a series on Martin Luther King.
sentences.zh: 所以我们做过一期关于马丁·路德·金的节目。

sentences.en: Lincoln has this ability to kind of channel a spirit of biblical prophecy and associate it with a brighter future for America.
sentences.zh: 林肯拥有这种能力，能够引导一种圣经预言的精神，并将其与美国更光明的未来联系起来。

sentences.en: But also, he seems to be fun.
sentences.zh: 而且，他似乎很有趣。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: He's an engaging, amusing person.
sentences.zh: 他是一个迷人、风趣的人。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And that combination of biblical prophet and somebody who would be fun to be with, they don't always gel, let's put it like that.
sentences.zh: 而圣经先知和这样一个有趣的人的结合，它们并不总是能融洽结合，我们这么说吧。

sentences.en: No, you're absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 不，你说得完全对。

sentences.en: And actually, you mentioned Daniel Day-Lewis.
sentences.zh: 事实上，你提到了丹尼尔·戴-刘易斯。

sentences.en: So Tabby, our producer, loves the Lincoln film and actually persuaded me to watch it a few weeks ago.
sentences.zh: 所以我们的制片人塔比很喜欢这部《林肯》电影，几周前还说服我去看了。

sentences.en: And Daniel Day-Lewis does bring this out in the Steven Spielberg film.
sentences.zh: 而在史蒂芬·斯皮尔伯格的电影中，丹尼尔·戴-刘易斯确实表现出了这一点。

sentences.en: There is a kind of whimsy to him, a folksiness.
sentences.zh: 他身上有一种古怪的魅力，一种平易近人的乡土气息。

sentences.en: Sometimes folksiness can be very annoying, but I think it's not terribly annoying in this film.
sentences.zh: 有时候这种乡土气息会让人很反感，但我认为在这部电影里并不是很烦人。

sentences.en: I think the last word should go to somebody who's one of Lincoln's great contemporaries.
sentences.zh: 我觉得应该把最后发言权留给林肯的伟大同代人之一。

sentences.en: Somebody who wasn't American, you know, didn't actually know that much about America, but was undoubtedly a great figure.
sentences.zh: 一个不是美国人的人，你知道，其实对美国没那么了解，但无疑是一个伟大的人物。

sentences.en: And that person, oddly, I think Michael Burlingham quotes him in his book, is Tolstoy.
sentences.zh: 而这个人，奇怪的是，我想迈克尔·伯林盖姆在他的书里引用过他，就是托尔斯泰。

sentences.en: So for the centenary of Lincoln's birth in 1909, the New York World sent a reporter to Tolstoy's estate,
sentences.zh: 所以在1909年林肯诞辰百年之际，《纽约世界报》派了一名记者去托尔斯泰的庄园，

sentences.en: Yasnaya Poliena, to ask Tolstoy, because they said, he's the world's greatest writer.
sentences.zh: 雅斯纳亚·波利亚纳，去问托尔斯泰，因为他们说，他是世界上最伟大的作家。

sentences.en: Let's see what he's got to say about Lincoln.
sentences.zh: 看看他对林肯有什么看法。

sentences.en: And this is what Tolstoy said.
sentences.zh: 这就是托尔斯泰所说的话。

sentences.en: He said, of all the great national heroes and statesmen of history, Lincoln is the only real giant.
sentences.zh: 他说，在历史上所有的伟大民族英雄和政治家中，林肯是唯一真正的巨人。

sentences.en: Alexander, Frederick the Great, Caesar, Napoleon, Gladstone, even Washington.
sentences.zh: 亚历山大、腓特烈大帝、恺撒、拿破仑、格莱斯顿，甚至华盛顿。

sentences.en: Frankly, I wouldn't put Washington in that list because you know my views on Washington with other people's teeth in his mouth.
sentences.zh: 坦白说，我不会把华盛顿列入这个名单，因为你知道我对华盛顿的看法，他嘴里塞着别人的假牙。

sentences.en: Even Washington.
sentences.zh: 甚至华盛顿。

sentences.en: They stand in greatness of character, in depth and feeling, and in certain moral power far behind Lincoln.
sentences.zh: 他们在性格的伟大、情感的深度以及某种道德力量上，都远远落后于林肯。

sentences.en: He came through many hardships and much experience to the realization that the greatest human achievement is love.
sentences.zh: 他经历了许多艰难险阻和丰富阅历，终于认识到人类最伟大的成就是爱。

sentences.en: He was what Beethoven was in music,
sentences.zh: 他之于音乐，正如贝多芬之于音乐，

sentences.en: Dante in poetry, Raphael in painting, and Christ in the philosophy of life.
sentences.zh: 但丁之于诗歌，拉斐尔之于绘画，基督之于人生哲学。

sentences.en: There's your Christ comparison, Tom.
sentences.zh: 这就是你的基督比喻，汤姆。

sentences.en: Lincoln was a man of whom a nation has a right to be proud.
sentences.zh: 林肯是一个让一个国家引以为豪的人。

sentences.en: He was a saint of humanity whose name will live thousands of years and the legends of future generations.
sentences.zh: 他是人类的圣人，他的名字将在未来世世代代的传说中活上数千年。

sentences.en: He lived and died a hero, and as a great character, he will live as long as the world lives.
sentences.zh: 他生为英雄，死为英雄，作为一个伟大的性格，他将与世界同在。

sentences.en: What a tone to end on.
sentences.zh: 以这样的基调收尾真不错。

sentences.en: Thank you, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，多米尼克。

sentences.en: That was fascinating.
sentences.zh: 这太迷人了。

sentences.en: Thank you, everyone, for listening.
sentences.zh: 谢谢大家的收听。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Hi, it's William Derimple here, again from Empire, another Goldhanger podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是威廉·达林普尔，再次来自Empire，另一个来自Goldhanger的播客。

sentences.en: Here's the clip from our recent series on the five partitions that created modern Asia.
sentences.zh: 这里是我们最近关于创造现代亚洲的五次分治系列的剪辑。

sentences.en: And it was deeply emotional.
sentences.zh: 而且这是极其感人的。

sentences.en: Sparsh picked up some pebbles from the village, which he made into jewellery, family heirlooms for his family going down the generations, because he was always saying,
sentences.zh: 斯帕什从村子里捡了一些鹅卵石，做成了首饰，作为他们家族代代相传的传家宝，因为他总是说，

sentences.en: you know, my family doesn't have archives, etc.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我的家族没有什么档案之类的。

sentences.en: We lost everything in partition.
sentences.zh: 我们在分治中失去了一切。

sentences.en: And there's nothing that we have from Bela to show where we came from.
sentences.zh: 我们没有什么东西可以从贝拉证明我们来自哪里。

sentences.en: But so he wanted to pick up something from Bela and make it into aliens for the next generations.
sentences.zh: 但他想从贝拉捡点东西，把它做成给后代的信物。

sentences.en: You know, three, four generations from now, they'll still have a piece of Bela with them, even if, you know, the relationship between India and Pakistan worsens again.
sentences.zh: 你知道，从现在开始的三四代人之后，他们身边依然会有一片贝拉的土地，即使，你知道，印度和巴基斯坦的关系再次恶化。

sentences.en: And, you know, even if his kids can never visit Bela, they'll always have a piece of Bela with them.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，即使他的孩子永远无法访问贝拉，他们身边也永远会有贝拉的一部分。

sentences.en: But this connection with earth,
sentences.zh: 但这种与大地的联系，

sentences.en: Dharati, you know, they call it Dharati in India.
sentences.zh: Dharati，你知道，他们在印度称之为Dharati。

sentences.en: And Zameen is the Urdu word for exactly the same thing.
sentences.zh: 而Zameen是乌尔都语中完全相同的词。

sentences.en: But it is much more than just the earth.
sentences.zh: 但这远不仅仅是泥土。

sentences.en: It is who you are, where you have grown from, where your forebears have grown from.
sentences.zh: 它是你是谁，你从哪里成长起来，你的祖先从哪里成长起来。

sentences.en: And the number of people I know who have been lucky enough to travel across the border, and I count myself as one, who find it impossible to leave without a scoop of earth.
sentences.zh: 我认识很多人，他们足够幸运能够跨越边界，我算其中一个，他们发现离开时如果没有带上一捧泥土是不可能的。

sentences.en: And I have one too.
sentences.zh: 我也有一个。

sentences.en: You know, in Lahore, picked up a handful of earth and brought it back with me.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，在拉合尔，捡了一把泥土并把它带了回来。

sentences.en: Because I thought, you know, this is the stuff my grandfather used to walk on.
sentences.zh: 因为我想，你知道，这就是我爷爷曾经走过的东西。
